section_summary: This section traces American, British, and Japanese negotiations over perpetual foreign leaseholds and the taxes associated with them. Britain and Japan move from conflicting proposals to an agreement ending the leases on April 1, 1942, while preserving existing tax exemptions until then; the United States accepts the same terms. The section also includes earlier treaty drafts, press notices, and a report on a separate leasehold settlement for St. Luke’s International Medical Center.

people.name: R. Walton Moore
people.role: Signed for the Secretary of State

people.name: Ishii
people.role: Delivered a treaty draft to the American Ambassador

people.name: Ito
people.role: Chairman of the Kobe Municipal Assembly’s Perpetual Lease Committee

people.name: F. Lindley
people.role: Former British representative in leasehold negotiations

subfiles.title: Conclusion of memorandum on perpetual leaseholds
subfiles.about: Assesses the claims and obligations of private American perpetual leaseholders.
subfiles.summary: Concludes that leaseholders’ rights are private and that their low rents may not cover municipal services.

subfiles.title: Annex A: Leaseholders’ contention that rent carried municipal tax exemption
subfiles.about: Examines whether purchase payments and ground rent exempted foreign leaseholders from municipal taxes.
subfiles.summary: Accepts the historical basis of the leaseholders’ argument but finds it unconvincing for services supplied by municipalities that grew beyond the former settlements.

subfiles.title: Annex B: Statement of the chairman of the Landrenters’ Committee
subfiles.about: Advocates ending perpetual leases through equitable purchase of leaseholders’ rights.
subfiles.summary: The chairman argues that differing land tenure perpetuates friction and urges equal treatment of foreign and Japanese residents.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1884: Perpetual leases
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports British efforts and compares proposed solutions to the perpetual lease dispute.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports stalled British discussions and the Japanese refusal to pay compensation. The Embassy favors a compensated buyout over the Department’s proposed conversion retaining some tax exemptions, while recognizing that Japan may reject compensation. He encloses three 1911 treaty or protocol drafts found in Embassy files.

subfiles.title: Enclosure 1: Draft second paragraph of Article XVI
subfiles.about: Proposes preserving existing perpetual lease rights until changed by mutual agreement.
subfiles.summary: Draft confirms existing leasehold rights, privileges, and immunities.

subfiles.title: Enclosure 2: Japan-form protocol
subfiles.about: Proposes maintaining American perpetual leases and treaty protections pending final settlement.
subfiles.summary: The draft preserves existing leases and protections under the 1894 treaty.

subfiles.title: Enclosure 3: Department-form protocol
subfiles.about: Sets out alternative language protecting leasehold rights during treaty replacement.
subfiles.summary: The draft maintains leases pending settlement and includes a pencilled Japanese suggestion against placing Americans in a less favorable position than other foreigners.

subfiles.title: The Perpetual Leases: Foreign Office and Collection of Taxes
subfiles.about: Reports plans to collect alleged tax arrears on perpetual leaseholds.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥1,340,000 in claimed arrears and lists leased areas by city.

subfiles.title: Instruction on settlement of perpetual leaseholds
subfiles.from: Department of State, signed by R. Walton Moore
subfiles.to: Erle R. Dickover, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Directs renewed discussions with Britain over an American leasehold settlement proposal.
subfiles.summary: The Department defends continued exemption from taxes on leased land and buildings, while requiring payment of other municipal charges. It considers a compensated buyout impractical and asks the Embassy to seek British support for its proposed settlement and report the response.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2067: Perpetual leases
subfiles.from: Erle R. Dickover, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits a new British proposal and reports Japanese municipal pressure to end the leases.
subfiles.summary: Britain proposes freehold conversion after 99 years, without compensation, and payment of disputed taxes; municipalities seek faster liquidation.

subfiles.title: British note No. 155 proposing leasehold settlement
subfiles.to: Hachiro Arita, Japanese Minister for Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: Offers three principles for settling British perpetual leaseholds.
subfiles.summary: Clive reviews failed efforts to obtain compensation. He proposes converting leases to freehold 99 years after grant, seeking no compensation or refunds, and paying disputed local taxes in future.

subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum on British proposal
subfiles.about: Recommends willingness to accept the new British proposal.
subfiles.summary: Argues that the United States should accept terms Britain is prepared to take and attaches a proposed telegram.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 138 on the British leasehold proposal
subfiles.about: Authorizes conditional American support for settlement on the British proposal’s terms.
subfiles.summary: The Department accepts the British basis if existing land and building tax exemptions continue during the 99-year period, while noting that individual legal rights remain enforceable.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 230 on Japanese counterproposal
subfiles.from: Erle R. Dickover, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Japan’s rejection of the 99-year proposal and its demand for rapid conversion.
subfiles.summary: Japan proposes conversion in April 1937 with five years’ exemption from national land tax, threatening tax collection if rejected. Dickover recommends awaiting British leaseholders’ views.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 143 approving delay
subfiles.about: Approves waiting before approaching Japan.
subfiles.summary: Approves the Embassy’s proposed delay.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2240: Perpetual leases
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese and British notes and a conversation memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Grew encloses three documents and plans to consult major American leaseholders.

subfiles.title: Japanese note No. 213 rejecting the 99-year proposal
subfiles.from: Hachiro Arita, Japanese Minister for Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: Presents Japan’s counterproposal for rapid termination of perpetual leases.
subfiles.summary: Arita argues that perpetual leases unfairly reduce foreign holders’ tax burden and have outlived their original purpose. Japan proposes uncompensated conversion in April 1937 and five years’ exemption from national land tax. The note threatens assessment of outstanding taxes and other measures if settlement fails.

subfiles.title: Conversation between Grew and Clive
subfiles.about: Records Clive’s planned five-year compromise and Grew’s initial response.
subfiles.summary: Clive reports reluctant British leaseholder consent; Grew promises to consult American holders.

subfiles.title: British note No. 9 proposing conversion in 1942
subfiles.to: Hachiro Arita, Japanese Minister for Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: Counters Japan’s April 1937 proposal with conversion on April 1, 1942.
subfiles.summary: Clive disputes Japan’s account of the leases’ legal history and defends vested rights. Seeking compromise, Britain proposes uncompensated conversion to freehold on April 1, 1942, with existing tax exemptions maintained and remaining disputed arrears waived until then.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 63 reporting Japanese acceptance
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese acceptance of the British proposal, pending Privy Council approval.
subfiles.summary: Grew requests guidance on encouraging American leaseholders to accept equivalent terms.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 36 authorizing American acceptance
subfiles.about: Authorizes the Embassy to accept settlement on the British–Japanese terms.
subfiles.summary: Directs oral notification and refers the Embassy to earlier guidance on American holders.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 70 reporting notification to Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports informal notice that the United States accepts the British settlement basis.
subfiles.summary: Grew preserves American holders’ legal rights, asks Japan to defer publicity, and recommends informing principal leaseholders.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 71 on draft notes and letters
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Explains the proposed note exchange and asks for authority to submit matching American drafts.
subfiles.summary: The accompanying letters clarify tax exemptions through March 1942 and preserve settlement terms after lease transfers.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 40 authorizing draft notes
subfiles.about: Authorizes submission of matching notes and consultation with American leaseholders.
subfiles.summary: Also directs explanation of London press reports and the Department’s need to issue a statement soon.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 74 advancing the draft deadline
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports an earlier deadline for submitting American drafts to the Privy Council.
subfiles.summary: Japan now requires the drafts by the following afternoon for March 17 consideration.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 73 requesting publicity guidance
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Asks where and when American acceptance should be publicized.
subfiles.summary: Reports that principal American leaseholders appear inclined to accept.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 43 on Department press release
subfiles.about: Reports issuance of a press release on American willingness to accept settlement.
subfiles.summary: The release reviews the negotiations and expresses hope that American holders accept.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 80 reporting draft submission
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Confirms submission of American draft settlement documents.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office sees no objection to immediate publicity in Washington.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 83 on Privy Council review
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports planned review and exchange of settlement documents.
subfiles.summary: Grew explains why he filed no formal reservation of American leaseholders’ individual rights.

subfiles.title: Statement for the press on perpetual lease settlement
subfiles.about: Announces American willingness to accept the British–Japanese settlement terms.
subfiles.summary: Says leases will end in April 1942 and expresses hope for holders’ cooperation.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 92 on signing and publicity
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports a March 25 exchange date and Japan’s wish for immediate publicity.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office plans to sign and exchange the documents at noon March 25.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 50 approving publicity
subfiles.about: Responds to Japan’s proposed publicity after the note exchange.
subfiles.summary: The Department raises no objection.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 97 confirming exchange
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Confirms signature and exchange of the settlement notes and letters.
subfiles.summary: Notes and letters were signed and exchanged at noon.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to the Secretary on the lease settlement
subfiles.about: Summarizes the settlement and credits Dooman’s work.
subfiles.summary: Calls the planned April 1942 conversion a diplomatic achievement after decades of friction.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on publicity for the settlement
subfiles.about: Reviews publicity already given and the expected exchange of notes.
subfiles.summary: Recommends awaiting the exchanged texts before further publication.

subfiles.title: Copy of March 6 press statement
subfiles.about: Repeats the Department’s announcement of the proposed settlement.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes April 1942 conversion and urges American leaseholders’ cooperation.

subfiles.title: Division note on despatch and four enclosures
subfiles.about: Calls attention to settlement drafts and the need for final signed texts.
subfiles.summary: Requests the exchanged texts before publication.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2319 transmitting settlement drafts
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits four draft notes and letters for the American–Japanese settlement.
subfiles.summary: Reports anticipated Privy Council approval and a March 25 exchange.

subfiles.title: Draft American note to Japanese Minister for Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: Sets out the proposed American–Japanese perpetual lease settlement.
subfiles.summary: Provides for uncompensated conversion on April 1, 1942, without registration taxes, while preserving tax exemptions and waiving disputed arrears until then.

subfiles.title: Draft American accompanying letter
subfiles.about: Clarifies the settlement’s tax and transfer provisions.
subfiles.summary: Limits pre-1942 tax collection and preserves agreement terms when a lease is transferred.

subfiles.title: Draft Japanese reply note
subfiles.about: Confirms the terms of the American–Japanese settlement.
subfiles.summary: Repeats and accepts the April 1942 conversion, tax exemption, and arrears provisions.

subfiles.title: Draft Japanese accompanying letter
subfiles.about: Confirms the tax and lease transfer clarifications.
subfiles.summary: Accepts the American letter’s interpretation of exemptions and transferred leases.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2384: St. Luke’s perpetual leasehold
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports St. Luke’s International Medical Center’s separate relinquishment of its Tokyo perpetual lease.
subfiles.summary: After Rudolph Teusler’s death, St. Luke’s incorporated under Japanese law and voluntarily relinquished its leasehold in July 1936. Tokyo authorities granted specified prefectural and municipal tax exemptions for ten years, a settlement the institution considered satisfactory.
